config.title: Monitoring & observability

intro.title: Monitoring & observability
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple monitoring dashboard to visualize system health metrics like CPU usage and memory consumption. You'll learn the core concepts of monitoring and observability, which involve collecting, tracking, and displaying data to understand how a system performs. The main technologies involved include using metrics data structures and basic visualization techniques to create real-time charts. By the end, you'll be able to implement a basic observability tool that helps in detecting and responding to system issues.
intro.usecase: Monitoring and observability are essential in production systems like e-commerce platforms, where dashboards track real-time metrics such as order processing rates, API response times, and error rates. Developers use tools like Grafana or Datadog to visualize system health through interactive panels that display latency graphs, error logs, and resource utilization. This enables teams to quickly identify and resolve issues like slow database queries or service outages, ensuring reliability and performance for end-users.

objectives: Construct a basic monitoring dashboard to visualize system metrics
Configure alert rules to trigger notifications based on predefined thresholds
Implement logging mechanisms to capture application events and errors
Integrate tracing tools to follow request flows across distributed components
Initialize metric collection for key performance indicators like latency and throughput
Apply aggregation techniques to summarize raw monitoring data into actionable insights
Manipulate visualization parameters to customize metric displays for different stakeholders
